calls.title: St. Louis got their looks
calls.plain: The Blues’ shots were at least as dangerous as usual.
calls.said: the Blues would get their usual good looks against a Ducks team that gives them up
calls.beyond: St. Louis usually gets some of the league’s most dangerous shots, and Anaheim usually gives up some of the league’s most dangerous shots. Even by those standards, this was a night of good looks: St. Louis’s shots at 5-on-5 had a 9.4% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.7% (about 7.3% against Anaheim) and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 15 games.

calls.head: The Ducks’ edge in physicality
calls.body: The Ducks are one of the league’s best for physicality, and the Blues are around the middle. It’s the widest gap between these two, though not a huge one.
calls.call: The Ducks hit more than the Blues in the close stretches of the game.

surprises.head: Anaheim hardly hit anyone
surprises.body: Anaheim is one of the league’s heaviest-hitting teams. Not tonight: a hit score of 58 in the close stretches of the game, against their usual 117 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 50 games.

story.head: The Blues survive a Ducks rally
paras: This one got way too interesting for the Blues. Jonatan Berggren opened the scoring for the Blues early in the first, but Alex Killorn tied it 1-1 for Anaheim midway through the period. Connor McMichael restored the Blues’ lead with just under a minute left in the period. The second period was a wild one. Cutter Gauthier tied it 2-2 for Anaheim early in the period. Robert Thomas and Dalibor Dvorský scored just under two minutes apart midway through the period to put the Blues up 4-2. Gauthier scored his 20th of the season on the power play less than three minutes later to pull the Ducks within one. The Blues scored four times in the third. Jake Neighbours, Philip Broberg and Logan Mailloux scored three goals in just under three minutes in the first half of the third to extend the lead to 7-3. Lukáš Dostál replaced Ville Husso in net for Anaheim in the third. Ian Moore made it 7-4 with just over five minutes left. With the goalie pulled and a minute and a half left, Mikael Granlund cut it to 7-5 on the power play. With the goalie still pulled and 41 seconds left, Gauthier completed his hat trick to pull the Ducks within one. Pavel Buchnevich shut the door with an empty-netter with 38 seconds left. Three players had three-point nights: Thomas with a goal and two assists, Mailloux with a goal and two assists, and the Ducks’ Jackson LaCombe with three assists.
The Blues had a bit more of the good stuff. Jordan Binnington made 25 saves for the Blues, and Husso allowed seven goals on 24 shots.
Colton Parayko and Jeff Malott picked up ten-minute misconducts. The Blues moved to 10-9-2, seventh in the Central, while the Ducks dropped to 11-10-1, third in the Pacific.

items.text: Robert Thomas tied Alex Pietrangelo for third on the Blues’ all-time assists list, with 341.
Cutter Gauthier has a point in twelve straight games, with a goal in each of the last ten.
Mason McTavish played his first game against Anaheim since leaving.
Robert Thomas scored again against Anaheim, and has seven goals in ten games against them since 2023-24.
